outline.topics: Logic and quantifiers, proof techniques, sets and events, indicator functions, limsup/liminf of sets, images and preimages, relations, countability, Cantor's diagonal argument
outline.read: Velleman, How to Prove It (3rd ed.); Hammack, Book of Proof (free)
outline.why: Preimages are what 'measurable' means later; countability is why probability is only countably additive.

outline.topics: Completeness, sequences, limsup and liminf, series, continuity, uniform convergence, compactness, metric spaces, Riemann integral, interchanging limits
outline.read: Abbott, Understanding Analysis (2nd ed.)
outline.problems: Abbott; Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis ch. 1-7
outline.why: Uniform convergence decides when you may truncate the uniformization series or differentiate under an integral.

outline.topics: Vector spaces, eigenvalues, Jordan form, spectral theorem, SVD, matrix norms, matrix exponential, nonnegative matrices, Perron-Frobenius, M-matrices, Kronecker products
outline.read: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right (4th ed., free)
outline.problems: Axler; Horn and Johnson, Matrix Analysis (2nd ed.)
outline.why: CTMC generators are M-matrices, stationary vectors come from Perron-Frobenius, and QBD generators are block-tridiagonal Kronecker sums.

outline.topics: Derivatives in R^n, chain rule, inverse and implicit function theorems, change of variables with Jacobians
outline.read: Rudin ch. 9-10 or Munkres, Analysis on Manifolds
outline.why: Jacobians give the density of transformed random variables, such as a passenger's wait as a function of two arrival times.

outline.topics: Sigma-algebras, pi-lambda theorem, Caratheodory extension, Lebesgue measure, measurable functions, monotone and dominated convergence, Fatou, Lp spaces, product measures, Fubini-Tonelli, Radon-Nikodym
outline.read: Axler, Measure, Integration & Real Analysis (free) or Tao, An Introduction to Measure Theory
outline.why: Likelihood-ratio gradient estimators are Radon-Nikodym derivatives; Fubini justifies swapping expectation and time integrals in your cost functions.

outline.topics: Convex sets and functions, LP duality, KKT conditions, Lagrangian duality, subgradients, SGD convergence
outline.read: Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization (free)
outline.problems: Boyd and Vandenberghe; Bertsimas and Tsitsiklis, Introduction to Linear Optimization
outline.why: The dispatch cost you minimize per time block is a constrained program; its dual variables are shadow prices, the starting point for tolls and surge pricing.

outline.topics: Normed, Banach and Hilbert spaces, Banach fixed-point theorem, orthogonal projection, bounded operators
outline.read: Kreyszig, Introductory Functional Analysis with Applications ch. 1-5
outline.why: Bellman operators are contractions on a Banach space; conditional expectation is a projection in L2.

outline.topics: Linear systems x' = Ax and the matrix exponential, existence and uniqueness, equilibria, linearization, Lyapunov functions, LaSalle; Laplace and Laplace-Stieltjes transforms with numerical inversion; Fourier transform and convolution; z-transforms
outline.read: Hirsch, Smale and Devaney, Differential Equations, Dynamical Systems, and an Introduction to Chaos (3rd ed.); Schiff, The Laplace Transform; Stein and Shakarchi, Fourier Analysis
outline.why: Kolmogorov's equations are a linear ODE system; stochastic approximation and fluid limits are judged by ODE stability; Laplace transforms give M/G/1 waiting-time distributions.

outline.topics: Heat and transport equations, method of characteristics, Kolmogorov backward and Fokker-Planck equations, the HJB equation
outline.read: Strauss, Partial Differential Equations: An Introduction (2nd ed.)
outline.why: Needed only for diffusion approximations (3.8) and mean-field games (6.6).

outline.topics: Counting, conditioning, Bayes, discrete and continuous random variables, joint and derived distributions, order statistics, transforms, informal limit theorems
outline.read: Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis, Introduction to Probability (2nd ed.)
outline.problems: MIT 6.041 problem sets; Blitzstein and Hwang, Introduction to Probability (free)
outline.why: Reliability of series and parallel systems; whether a passenger group finds a large-enough taxi.

outline.topics: Axioms, Caratheodory, Lebesgue measure on [0,1], infinite coin toss, independence of sigma-algebras, Borel-Cantelli lemmas, Kolmogorov 0-1 law, discrete, continuous and singular distributions
outline.read: Jagannathan's NPTEL notes, modules 0-2; Rosenthal, A First Look at Rigorous Probability Theory (2nd ed.)
outline.problems: Grimmett and Stirzaker, One Thousand Exercises in Probability (3rd ed.)
outline.why: Thinning and superposition of taxi arrival streams; Borel-Cantelli decides whether the buffer empties infinitely often.

outline.topics: Expectation as a Lebesgue integral; Markov, Chebyshev, Jensen, Holder, Minkowski and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities; transformations with Jacobians; PGF, MGF, characteristic functions; inversion and uniqueness; multivariate normal
outline.read: Grimmett and Stirzaker, Probability and Random Processes (4th ed.) ch. 3-5; Jagannathan's notes, modules 3-4
outline.problems: One Thousand Exercises; Shiryaev, Problems in Probability
outline.why: Chernoff bounds on the chance a time block overflows the taxi buffer.

outline.topics: Four modes of convergence, uniform integrability, Skorokhod representation, continuous mapping, Slutsky, weak and strong laws, Levy continuity, Lindeberg-Feller CLT, Poisson limit, delta method, Cramer's theorem
outline.read: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples (5th ed.) ch. 2-3; Jagannathan's notes, module 5
outline.why: Monte Carlo error bars, and how fast your simulated daily costs converge.

outline.topics: Definition via Radon-Nikodym, properties, L2 projection, regular conditional distributions, conditional independence
outline.read: Williams, Probability with Martingales ch. 9
outline.why: Expected wait given the current queue state is the quantity every dispatch policy optimizes.

outline.topics: Filtrations, stopping times, optional stopping, Doob's inequalities, martingale convergence, uniformly integrable martingales, Wald's identity, Azuma-Hoeffding, Hoeffding, Bernstein, McDiarmid
outline.read: Williams ch. 10-14; Vershynin, High-Dimensional Probability ch. 2 (free)
outline.why: Wald's identity for dispatches until the queue clears; optional stopping for the buffer hitting zero before K.

outline.topics: Chi-square, t and F distributions, order statistics, sufficiency, factorization theorem, minimal sufficiency, completeness, exponential families, ancillarity, Basu's theorem
outline.read: Casella and Berger, Statistical Inference (2nd ed.) ch. 5-6
outline.why: When is the count of taxi arrivals in a block sufficient for its rate?

outline.topics: Method of moments, MLE, Bayes estimators, EM algorithm, MSE, Fisher information, Cramer-Rao, Rao-Blackwell, Lehmann-Scheffe
outline.read: Casella and Berger ch. 7
outline.why: MLE and Cramer-Rao bounds for hourly arrival rates from airport logs.

outline.topics: Neyman-Pearson, UMP tests, monotone likelihood ratio, likelihood-ratio, Wald and score tests, p-values, multiple testing, pivots, inverting tests
outline.read: Casella and Berger ch. 8-9
outline.why: Test whether taxi interarrival times are exponential, or whether a flight bank shifts the rate.

outline.topics: Consistency, asymptotic normality and efficiency of the MLE, delta method, Wilks' theorem, M-estimators
outline.read: Casella and Berger ch. 10; van der Vaart, Asymptotic Statistics
outline.problems: Casella and Berger; van der Vaart
outline.why: Delta-method error bars on derived quantities such as the mean wait 1/(mu - lambda).

outline.topics: OLS geometry, Gauss-Markov, inference for coefficients, GLMs including Poisson regression, regularization
outline.read: Wasserman, All of Statistics ch. 13; James et al., ISLP (free)
outline.why: Poisson regression of passenger demand on flight arrivals, hour and weekday.

outline.topics: Priors, conjugacy, hierarchical models, Metropolis-Hastings, Gibbs sampling, bootstrap, kernel density estimation, cross-validation
outline.read: Wasserman; Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis (3rd ed., free)
outline.why: Bayesian updating of the demand rate for dynamic pricing; bootstrap intervals for policy cost.

outline.topics: Rate estimation for nonhomogeneous Poisson processes, goodness-of-fit for interarrival times, MLE of a CTMC generator, phase-type fitting by EM, batch means and simulation output intervals
outline.read: Law, Simulation Modeling and Analysis; Asmussen and Glynn, Stochastic Simulation
outline.why: Fit the arrival model your CTMC needs, then state confidence intervals for simulated daily cost.

outline.topics: Classification, hitting times, stationary distributions, ergodic theorem, reversibility, coupling, mixing times, MCMC convergence
outline.read: Norris, Markov Chains ch. 1; Levin and Peres, Markov Chains and Mixing Times (2nd ed., free)
outline.why: Mixing-time bounds tell you how long your simulation's warm-up must be.

outline.topics: Homogeneous, nonhomogeneous, compound and marked Poisson processes; thinning and superposition; renewal theory and the key renewal theorem; renewal-reward; regenerative processes; inspection paradox; Little's law
outline.read: Gallager, Stochastic Processes: Theory for Applications; Ross, Stochastic Processes (2nd ed.)
outline.why: Flight-driven nonhomogeneous arrivals; renewal-reward for long-run cost per taxi.

outline.topics: Generators, Kolmogorov equations, explosion, embedded chain, uniformization, birth-death chains, reversibility, transient analysis, phase-type distributions
outline.read: Norris ch. 2-3; Kulkarni, Modeling and Analysis of Stochastic Systems (3rd ed.)
outline.why: A uniformization truncation bound you can put in your paper, rather than a fixed number of terms.

outline.topics: M/M/c/K, Erlang B and C, M/G/1 and Pollaczek-Khinchine, PASTA, Jackson and BCMP networks, time-varying queues, fluid and diffusion limits, double-ended matching queues
outline.read: Harchol-Balter, Performance Modeling and Design of Computer Systems; Whitt, Stochastic-Process Limits (free)
outline.why: The taxi stand as a double-ended queue with passenger impatience.

outline.topics: Quasi-birth-death processes, matrix-geometric solution, R and G matrices, logarithmic and cyclic reduction, level-dependent QBDs, Markovian arrival processes
outline.read: Latouche and Ramaswami, Introduction to Matrix Analytic Methods in Stochastic Modeling; Neuts, Matrix-Geometric Solutions in Stochastic Models
outline.problems: Latouche and Ramaswami; Stewart, Probability, Markov Chains, Queues, and Simulation
outline.why: Your taxi-buffer x passenger-queue model is a QBD: compute R and check it against your transient solver.

outline.topics: Random variate generation, discrete-event simulation, common random numbers, control variates, importance sampling, finite differences, SPSA, IPA, likelihood-ratio gradients
outline.read: Asmussen and Glynn, Stochastic Simulation: Algorithms and Analysis; Spall, Introduction to Stochastic Search and Optimization
outline.why: Compare SPSA, IPA and likelihood-ratio gradients of block cost with respect to dispatch parameters.

outline.topics: Robbins-Monro, Kiefer-Wolfowitz, the ODE method, step-size conditions, two-timescale and asynchronous stochastic approximation
outline.read: Borkar, Stochastic Approximation: A Dynamical Systems Viewpoint (2nd ed.); Kushner and Yin
outline.why: Convergence conditions for SPSA and Adam-like steps on your objective; two-timescale pricing plus dispatch.

outline.topics: Brownian motion, quadratic variation, Ito integral and formula, SDEs, reflected Brownian motion, Girsanov
outline.read: Le Gall, Brownian Motion, Martingales, and Stochastic Calculus
outline.why: Diffusion approximations of the taxi queue in heavy traffic.

outline.topics: Sparse direct and iterative solvers for stationary distributions (GTH, power, Gauss-Seidel, GMRES), conditioning and error bounds, computing the matrix exponential (uniformization, Pade approximants, Krylov methods), stiffness and ODE integrators, block methods for QBDs, GPU sparse kernels
outline.read: Stewart, Introduction to the Numerical Solution of Markov Chains; Trefethen and Bau, Numerical Linear Algebra; Moler and Van Loan, 'Nineteen Dubious Ways to Compute the Exponential of a Matrix, Twenty-Five Years Later' (SIAM Review, 2003)
outline.why: Puts error bounds and theory under the sparse, GPU-accelerated transient solver you already run, and tells you when uniformization beats an ODE integrator.

outline.topics: Principle of optimality, backward induction, inventory problems, optimal stopping, one-step look-ahead rules
outline.read: Bertsekas, Dynamic Programming and Optimal Control Vol. I (4th ed.); Ross, Introduction to Stochastic Dynamic Programming
outline.why: Time-block dispatch and pricing over a day as a finite-horizon problem.

outline.topics: Bellman operator, contraction, value iteration, policy iteration, modified policy iteration, LP formulation, occupation measures
outline.read: Puterman, Markov Decision Processes ch. 6
outline.why: Solve a small taxi-release MDP by value iteration, policy iteration and LP, and check they agree.

outline.topics: Unichain and multichain models, average-cost optimality equation, relative value iteration, vanishing discount, Blackwell optimality
outline.read: Puterman ch. 8-9; Bertsekas Vol. II (4th ed.)
outline.why: Long-run average cost per hour is the natural criterion for a stand that runs all day.

outline.topics: Monotone policies, submodularity, threshold policies, admission, routing and dispatch control, semi-Markov and continuous-time MDPs via uniformization, countable-state conditions
outline.read: Puterman ch. 11; Sennott, Stochastic Dynamic Programming and the Control of Queueing Systems
outline.why: Prove the optimal taxi-release rule is a threshold in the passenger queue.

outline.topics: Lagrangian methods, constrained occupation-measure LPs, randomized optimal policies, belief-state MDPs
outline.read: Altman, Constrained Markov Decision Processes; Krishnamurthy, Partially Observed Markov Decision Processes
outline.why: Minimize taxi idling subject to a cap on passenger wait or blocking.

outline.topics: Value-function approximation, post-decision states, rollout, aggregation, approximate LP
outline.read: Powell, Approximate Dynamic Programming (2nd ed.) or Reinforcement Learning and Stochastic Optimization; Bertsekas Vol. II
outline.why: City-wide repositioning is too large for exact DP; ADP with post-decision states is the standard route.

outline.topics: Single-product dynamic pricing (Gallego-van Ryzin), intensity control, customer choice models including multinomial logit, network revenue management and bid prices, deterministic LP bounds, pricing while learning demand
outline.read: Gallego and Topaloglu, Revenue Management and Pricing Analytics; Talluri and van Ryzin, The Theory and Practice of Revenue Management
outline.why: Your research includes dynamic pricing: this is the theory of setting time-varying prices against random demand, the base for surge pricing at the stand.

outline.topics: Deterministic optimal control, Pontryagin's maximum principle, the HJB equation, fluid models of time-varying queues and their optimal control
outline.read: Liberzon, Calculus of Variations and Optimal Control Theory; Bertsekas, Dynamic Programming and Optimal Control Vol. I (deterministic continuous-time chapter)
outline.why: Smooth fluid approximations of the full-day dispatch problem, solvable with ODE methods.

outline.topics: Monte Carlo, TD(lambda), SARSA, Q-learning, eligibility traces, exploration
outline.read: Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (2nd ed., free)
outline.why: Q-learning on your taxi-release MDP, checked against the exact solution.

outline.topics: Q-learning and TD as stochastic approximation, linear function approximation, the deadly triad, gradient-TD
outline.read: Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis, Neuro-Dynamic Programming; Szepesvari, Algorithms for Reinforcement Learning (free); Meyn, Control Systems and Reinforcement Learning
outline.why: Prove your tabular learner converges using the ODE method.

outline.topics: UCB, Thompson sampling, regret lower bounds, linear and contextual bandits, bandits for pricing
outline.read: Lattimore and Szepesvari, Bandit Algorithms (free)
outline.why: Posted-price surge as a bandit: learn the demand curve while pricing.

outline.topics: Policy gradient theorem, baselines and variance reduction, natural policy gradient, TRPO and PPO, two-timescale actor-critic
outline.read: Agarwal, Jiang, Kakade and Sun, Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Algorithms (free); Konda and Tsitsiklis on actor-critic
outline.why: PPO for dispatch with a continuous release rate per block.

outline.topics: PAC bounds, generative-model sample complexity, linear MDPs, offline RL basics
outline.read: Agarwal, Jiang, Kakade and Sun
outline.why: How many simulated days a learner needs to be near-optimal on your model.

outline.topics: DQN and PPO in practice, RL for queueing networks, ride-hailing dispatch and repositioning, multi-agent RL
outline.read: Dai and Gluzman, Stochastic Systems 2022; Qin et al., INFORMS J. Applied Analytics 2020; Lin et al., KDD 2018
outline.problems: Replicate one paper's experiment at small scale
outline.why: Average-cost deep RL for the taxi stand, benchmarked against the threshold policy.

outline.read: Maschler, Solan and Zamir, Game Theory (2nd ed.); Osborne and Rubinstein, A Course in Game Theory (free)

outline.read: Maschler, Solan and Zamir; Filar and Vrieze, Competitive Markov Decision Processes
outline.why: Repeated interaction between drivers and the dispatcher.

outline.read: Roughgarden, Twenty Lectures on Algorithmic Game Theory; Nisan et al., Algorithmic Game Theory (free)
